name: Boonie hat

lead: The boonie hat is a lightweight hat with a stiffer, all-round brim and a soft crown, originally military headwear for hot climates. Its brim shades the face, ears and neck, which is how it supports skin health and, over time, a more even, less sun-damaged complexion.
It is also worn as a style piece, and a few T Nation posters mention it as a way to cover a sunburn-prone bald scalp. No studies have tested it specifically.

paras: People wear it outdoors in place of a cap, often with a chin cord or drawstring in wind. One poster describes a Columbia mesh-top boonie as a way to protect a bald scalp after building up a tan gradually; the hat softens with washing and packs into a pocket.
The hat carries no special risks; its coverage is limited to the areas under the brim, so other exposed skin still receives sun.

angle.text: The brim reduces direct sun on the face and neck. Wearers also adopt it as a casual style item.

lead: The boonie hat is a wide-brimmed sun hat with a soft crown, a stitched brim, ventilation eyelets and often a chin strap or foliage loops. It originated as tropical military headwear.[1][2]

For appearance, it matters mainly as sun protection for the face, ears and neck, areas where cumulative sun exposure shows up as skin ageing. It is also worn as part of outdoor and military-inspired style.
Bald and thinning-haired men on fitness forums mention it as a way to shield the scalp from sunburn.[3]

paras: The boonie hat combines a crushable crown with a stitched brim, ventilation eyelets and an adjustable cord.[1] Its forerunners include tropical hats from the late 1930s. US forces were issued the modern version during the Vietnam War, from 1967, and the name derives from "boondocks".[2][1]

A T Nation poster with a bald scalp described gradually tanning his head for 30-40 minutes, then wearing a Columbia boonie with a mesh top and wide brim; he noted it softens with washing and packs away easily.[3]

timeline.event: "Johnny Jeep" wide-brim hats become a fashion fad in the US.[2]
US Army begins issuing the boonie hat.[2]
